notes: Translated from OVAL access_control/duty1-3. OVAL's state of the world is an event log; the compensate row becomes one evidence record with its payAmount as an evidence parameter, and the play row is the request. OVAL's request names no party; the log's actor, ex:William_Hall, is made the assignee, so the duty's bearer is defined (the duty and its permission name no assignee, so the bearer is the request subject, workflows §5.3). OVAL's separate permission for compensate exists to make the payment event itself compliant in monitoring mode. At f0839f6 it had no target (IM 2.6.1) and was dropped; upstream gave it one, document:1234, in 531edf1, and the log's compensate row the same object, so both are kept. The permission does not match the play request, and the duty has no relation, so the evidence's object is not consulted (workflows §5.3). Upstream also made the policy a Set (c2773ed), which changes nothing here. odrl:unit was a string literal; IM 2.5.1 makes it an IRI. This is the first corpus case with a witness-source operand, written as OVAL writes it: a refinement of the duty's action. due2-core binds odrl:payAmount to the witness source (due2-profiles.md §9 #6, resolved 2026-10-11), so the policy carries no binding of its own and the refinement is an ordinary witness condition. OVAL parameterises duties: under its default (semantics_for_duties=1) a permission with an unfulfilled duty is granted on the promise of performance (duty2: True); under -1 it is refused (duty3: False). due2 has one reading — Pending, naming the duty — which agrees with neither as a yes/no but is what both are approximating. duty2 and duty3 have identical inputs, so they are one scenario here. OVAL's refinement states odrl:unit Euro, a unit due2-core's odrl:payAmount does not declare (currencies vary), so W1 admits the policy with the warning UncheckedUnit and the witness condition is U with status misfit whatever amount the payment states (decisions/0049). duty1 and duty2/duty3, whose duty a payment is evidence for, are therefore Indeterminate between Pending and Permit, where OVAL compares the amounts and answers accept; the scenario with no payment keeps its Pending. A policy that needs the amount checked binds an operand of its own that declares due2:unit.

expected.why: ex:policy:88#play applies. ev-pay is a compensate by the bearer before effective_at, but the refinement's unit Euro is one odrl:payAmount's binding does not declare, so the condition on its payAmount 6.1 is U (misfit) and the duty's fulfilled finding is U: Permit where the payment counts, Pending where it does not. Indeterminate, Pending..Permit.

ex:policy:88#play applies. ev-pay is the only candidate witness; its payAmount 2 would fail ≥ 5.0, but the unit Euro is one the binding does not declare, so the condition is U (misfit) whatever the amount, and the duty's fulfilled finding is U: Indeterminate, Pending..Permit.
No evidence at all: the duty has no witness, which is F, not U (§5.3). Pending with the same single route.
